quote_or_paraphrase: "in about fifty years' time it will be possible to programme computers, with a storage capacity of about 10^9, to make them play the imitation game so well that an average interrogator will not have more than 70 per cent chance of making the right identification after five minutes"
source: Turing A.M. (1950) Computing Machinery and Intelligence, Mind 59:433-460, https://doi.org/10.1093/mind/LIX.236.433

quote_or_paraphrase: "more probable than not that, within the twentieth century, an ultraintelligent machine will be built"
source: Good I.J. (1965) Speculations Concerning the First Ultraintelligent Machine, Advances in Computers 6:31-88, https://doi.org/10.1016/S0065-2458(08)60418-0
note: 'more probable than not by 2000' -> median <= 2000; 2000 used

target: any work a man can do
quote_or_paraphrase: "machines will be capable, within twenty years, of doing any work a man can do"
source: Simon H.A. (1965) The Shape of Automation for Men and Management, Harper & Row, p. 96

quote_or_paraphrase: "Within a generation ... the problem of creating 'artificial intelligence' will substantially be solved"
source: Minsky M. (1967) Computation: Finite and Infinite Machines, Prentice-Hall, p. 2

target: general intelligence of an average human
quote_or_paraphrase: "In from three to eight years we will have a machine with the general intelligence of an average human being"
source: Darrach B. (1970) Meet Shaky, the first electronic person, Life magazine, 20 Nov 1970, p. 58D
note: Minsky later said he was misquoted

quote_or_paraphrase: most common answer: about 50 years (many said more)
source: Michie D. (1973) Machines and the theory of intelligence, Nature 241:507-512, https://doi.org/10.1038/241507a0
note: median/modal answer as recalled (AI Impacts summarises this survey); exact distribution not re-checked

quote_or_paraphrase: "Within thirty years, we will have the technological means to create superhuman intelligence" ... "I'll be surprised if this event occurs before 2005 or after 2030"
source: Vinge V. (1993) The Coming Technological Singularity, VISION-21 Symposium, NASA CP-10129, https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/19940022856

quote_or_paraphrase: "the required hardware will be available in cheap machines in the 2020s"
source: Moravec H. (1998) When will computer hardware match the human brain? J. Evolution and Technology 1, https://www.jetpress.org/volume1/moravec.htm
note: hardware milestone rather than AGI itself; 2025 = midpoint of 2020s

quote_or_paraphrase: case for superhuman AI "within the first third of the next century"
source: Bostrom N. (1998) How Long Before Superintelligence? Int. J. Futures Studies 2, https://nickbostrom.com/superintelligence
note: upper bound (2033) used as the point

quote_or_paraphrase: computers will pass the Turing test by 2029
source: Kurzweil R. (1999) The Age of Spiritual Machines, Viking; restated in the 2002 Kurzweil-Kapor Long Bet

quote_or_paraphrase: fourth-generation universal robots with human-level capability around 2040
source: Moravec H. (1999) Robot: Mere Machine to Transcendent Mind, Oxford University Press
Kurzweil R. (2005) The Singularity Is Near, Viking

quote_or_paraphrase: log-normal distribution with mode 2025 and mean 2028 (first given 2009, restated Dec 2011)
source: Legg S. (2011) Tick, tock, tick, tock... BING, vetta.org blog, http://www.vetta.org/2011/12/goodbye-2011-hello-2012/
